title: New Lock Stoplogs
description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE. THIS IS NOT THE REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, NOR INFORMATION FOR BID. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District intends to solicit for the New Lock Stoplogs to provide fabrication services to the Soo Project Office (SPO) in Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The USDA is committed to issuing solicitations and awarding contracts in a fair and prompt manner. The Ombudsman Program for Agency Protests (OPAP) was established to address protest issues within the agency, providing an alternative to costly and time-consuming litigation. Operating independently, OPAP offers relief comparable to that granted by the Government Accountability Office (GAO). Interested parties are encouraged to resolve concerns through USDA�s internal Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) process before pursuing external forums such as the GAO. Concerns may be addressed informally or through a formal agency protest filed with either the Contracting Officer or the Ombudsman. Informal Forum with the Ombudsman 1. Initial Point of Contact: Interested parties who believe a specific USDA procurement is unfair or otherwise defective should first direct their concerns to the applicable Contracting Officer. 2. Escalation: If the Contracting Officer is unable to address their concerns, interested parties are encouraged to contact the USDA Ombudsman for Agency Protests. Under this informal process, the agency is not required to suspend contract award performance. Utilization of the informal forum does not suspend any time requirement for filing a formal protest with the agency or other forums. 3. Required Information: To ensure a timely response, interested parties should provide the following information to the Ombudsman: solicitation/contract number, contracting office, Contracting Officer, and solicitation closing date (if applicable). Formal Agency Protest with the Ombudsman 1. Effort to Resolve: Prior to submitting a formal agency protest, protesters must first use their best efforts to resolve their concerns with the Contracting Officer through open and frank discussions. 2. Independent Review: If the protester�s concerns remain unresolved, an Independent Review is available by the Ombudsman. The protester may file a formal agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or, alternatively, with the Ombudsman under the OPAP program. Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined in writing to be in the best interest of the Government. 3. Resolution Timeline: The agency�s goal is to resolve protests within 35 calendar days from the date of filing. 4. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104(a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. 5. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. 6. Submission: Formal protests under the OPAP program should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Election of Forum. By initiating a protest with the USDA, the protester agrees not to pursue the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If a protest is filed externally, the agency protest will be dismissed.

title: P110 CAPE CANAVERAL RAILHEAD AND TRANSFER FACILITIES AT KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLORIDA
description: PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS NOTICE ONLY: THE SOLICITATION WILL BE AVAILABLE ON OR ABOUT NOVEMBER 5, 2026, AT HTTPS://SAM.GOV/. THE SOLICITATION NUMBER IS N6945027R0006, FOR THE DESIGN-BID-BUILD (DBB) CONSTRUCTION PROJECT, P110 CAPE CANAVERAL RAILHEAD AND TRANSFER FACILITIES, KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLORIDA PROJECT TITLE: DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT, FY27, P110 CAPE CANAVERAL RAILHEAD AND TRANSFER FACILITIES, KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLORIDA PSC: Y1LB - Construction of Highways, Roads, Streets, Bridges, and Railways NAICS: 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. Project Description: The project will include but is not limited to the following: Constructs railroad trackage to connect and facilitate the transfer from commercial rail to the on-base processing facility at Cape Canaveral. Constructs a low-rise open air standing seam-metal roofed canopy on a reinforced shallow foundation with wide-flange beams and columns and continuous footings for a Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile Processing Facility (Motor Transfer Facility). Functions include receiving and shipping missile motors, components and Active Inert Missiles (AIMS) which require superflat floors for air pallet operations. The roof structure will include sloped, uninsulated metal roof panels on steel joists. The estimated Period of Performance is 527 calendar days. The best value continuum source selection process to be used for this acquisition is the tradeoff approach, as described in FAR 15.103-1. The best value tradeoff process is appropriate and permits evaluation of proposals based on price competition, technical merit, confidence assessment and other factors; permits impartial and comprehensive evaluation of offeror proposals; permits discussions if necessary; and ensures selection of the source whose performance provides the best value to the Government. A sources sought notice was posted to sam.gov on September 10, 2026 requesting small business industry interested and capability statement. Based on responses from the notice it was determined that the requirement should be issued as full and open. The solicitation will be a negotiated DBB acquisition. Proposals will be solicited in a two part submission for a single solicitation. The solicitation will utilize source selection procedures, which require offerors to submit a technical proposal, past performance and experience information, and a price proposal for evaluation by the Government. Award will be made to the offeror whose total price and technical proposal offer the best value to the Government. Competition Requirements: Unrestricted basis, under full and open competition. Procurement Method: FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. Type of Contract: Firm-Fixed Price The NAICS code for this construction solicitation is 237990 with a size standard of $45,000,000. Project Magnitude is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. This is a new procurement. It does not replace an existing contract. No prior contract information exists. Large business concerns will be required to submit a subcontracting plan prior to award of the contract. A Site Visit will be held for those offerors who choose to participate (exact date and time will be specified in the solicitation). Proposals will be due no earlier than 30 days after the solicitation is released (exact date and time will be specified in the solicitation). This will be an electronic solicitation, which can be downloaded from Sam.gov Opportunities at https://sam.gov/. The solicitation will be available at this site no earlier than 15 days after this pre-solicitation notice is posted. Offerors are responsible for checking the Sam.gov website for the solicitation and any subsequent amendments that may be issued. NO CONTRACT AWARD WILL BE MADE TO ANY CONTRACTOR THAT IS NOT REGISTERED OR IN THE PROCESS OF REGISTERING WITH THE SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM). PLEASE VISIT THE SAM WEBSITE AT https://www.sam.gov FOR INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO REGISTER.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK Sterile Processing Service ST-108 Testing Requirements Upgrade The contractor shall provide all the following for testing the water for/within SPS per the ANSI/AAMI ST108:2023 at the Marion, Fort Wayne, and Jackie Walorski VA sites as defined in this Statement of Work (SOW). WORK TO BE PERFORMED: Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, lodging, and supervision necessary to collect appropriate samples and deliver to a lab meeting the requirements for processing of AAMI ST108. Contractor shall calibrate the conductivity/resistivity meter monthly during their testing visit and provide a water analysis report. The contractor will be part of the multidisciplinary team that assists the water working group with resolving out-of-range water testing, in addition to: Serves as the subject matter expert on water testing per the ST108:2023 Serves as the subject matter expert on corrective actions to mitigate risks for out-of-range water testing parameters. Completes monthly, quarterly, and yearly testing per ST108:2023 and the VHA water contract/SOW. Completes performance qualification testing per the ST108:2023 and per the VHA contract/SOW. The contractor must report any outliers identified during testing within 24 hours of receiving laboratory results. Completes follow-up testing as ordered by engineering for out-of-range water parameters per the ST108:2023 and VHA water contract/SOW. The contractor shall provide VA end users with access to web-based reporting software for ongoing review of water testing data, historical trends, and compliance documentation. All reports must clearly highlight or delineate outliers and be designed to provide ease of reading, ensuring information is presented in a clear, organized, and actionable format. Contractor shall provide consultative services as needed, such as resolving abnormal water testing results, water system analysis, and mitigation of test results. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of Title 10, U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1, �Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements�. title: RFI: Fort Wolters H Barracks
description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought (RFI) � Fort Wolters H Barracks, Mineral Wells, Texas DISCLAIMER. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market intelligence, information, and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), or a commitment by the Government to write, issue, or award an agreement. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All response costs will be borne solely by the interested party. PURPOSE. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. ACQUISITION STRATEGY & NON-FAR MODEL. Statutory Authority: This project will potentially be executed as a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) or Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) project utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Non-FAR Environment: Prospective partners are advised that the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) does NOT apply to this procurement. The negotiated, bilateral Other Transaction Agreement will serve as the sole governing contract. Standard FAR clauses are inapplicable, though federal statutory constraints (such as federal fiscal law, criminal statutes, and general civil laws) remain fully applicable. Phased Agreement Mechanics: PBD Procurement Process: Phase 1, Design & Pre-Construction Services, a design-builder will be selected through a qualifications-based selection (QBS) process. The government will then negotiate a fee for Phase 1 services. There is no requirement to submit price proposals or design concepts during the initial selection. Phase 2, Final Design & Construction, is executed via a bilateral modification to the OT Agreement upon successful negotiation of a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) at approximately 65% design maturity. The Agreement contains an "off-ramp" clause allowing the Government to retain the design and procure construction separately if GMP negotiations fail. DBtB Procurement Process: Solicitation and evaluation during Phase 1 focuses on the qualifications, past performance, and integrated Design-Build experience of each offeror. The Government is evaluating the team and not necessarily how the offeror will design the structure. The Phase 1 evaluation results in the selection of three of the most highly qualified, competitive teams to proceed to Phase 2. Phase 2, the Government will issue the final RFP exclusively to the down-selected teams. This RFP includes the validated, performance-based requirements, establishes the firm Construction Cost Limit (CCL), and clearly defines the basic scope. Note: See link to provide industry feedback https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/ZQ8Rm8MaN7

title: DA01--VA-27-00015330 - Mission-Oriented Services for Application Integration and Capabilities (MOSAIC)
description: Request for Information Request for information Page 1 of 2 DESCRIPTION Request for Information Synopsis Mission-Oriented Services for Application Integration and Capabilities (MOSAIC) Enterprise Data Products, API Delivery, Data Access and Sharing 1.0 RFI Synopsis Narrative Background and Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), is conducting market research to inform a planned future acquisition known as Mission-Oriented Services for Application Integration and Capabilities (MOSAIC). MOSAIC is focused on positioning VA s authoritative data as a trustworthy, well-structured enterprise asset that can be reliably consumed in whatever form the mission requires. VA seeks to continuously improve this data so that it can be relied upon as genuinely authoritative and to make that same data available through the full range of access patterns the mission requires: real-time transactional APIs, bulk and analytical access suitable for data-lake and large-scale workloads, event-driven and streaming exchange, and the governed, well-described, AI-ready data products that models, agents, and automated features increasingly require. A single data domain today may be served reliably through one interface yet remain difficult to access in another or exposed broadly while portions of its underlying content are known to be incomplete or unreliable. The VA intends for MOSAIC to close these gaps so that the same trusted data can be accessed, reused, and acted upon across many mission and technology use cases. VA is using this RFI to better understand how this mission should evolve over the next five to ten years and what technical, operating, and acquisition decisions made today would best position VA for that future. VA currently supports mission data and integration products that may form part of the initial MOSAIC baseline, including VA Profile, VADIR, HDR, existing API products, and related integration capabilities. The final inventory, transition boundaries, and allocation of work among MOSAIC, VA organizations, and other enterprise contracts have not been determined. MOSAIC will also operate in an environment that depends on enterprise data platforms, catalogs, identity services, infrastructure, security capabilities, and other agency- or vendor-managed services. VA does not want this market research to assume that today's API, integration, architecture, delivery, or operating models should simply be carried forward. VA is specifically seeking industry's perspective on how AI agents, real-time data access, event-driven architecture, interoperability standards, reusable data products, automation, and other emerging technologies may change the way VA exposes, exchanges, governs, and operates mission data. VA also wants industry to identify capabilities, architecture patterns, tools, and operating practices that should be reduced, retired, consolidated, or replaced as the ecosystem evolves. This RFI is intended to inform the MOSAIC Performance Work Statement (PWS), technical and operating model, transition approach, performance framework, commercial structure, acquisition strategy, and source-selection design. VA has not made final decisions regarding the future-state architecture, delivery model, single- versus multiple-award structure, contract type, ordering approach, period of performance, ceiling, pricing model, or final technical evaluation factors. Industry is encouraged to challenge VA's current assumptions and recommend alternatives supported by demonstrated operational, technical, and commercial experience. Areas for Industry Perspective VA is seeking forward-looking industry perspective on the following areas rather than validation of a predetermined solution: The future state VA should pursue over the next five to ten years for positioning its authoritative data as a trustworthy, well-structured, multi-modal enterprise asset, including the capabilities and architectural principles that should define that target state. How AI agents, event-driven and real-time data patterns, interoperability standards, data products, automation, and emerging technologies may change the role of traditional APIs, point-to-point integrations, middleware, and manual integration services. Which current capabilities, technical patterns, tools, and operating practices VA should plan to eliminate, consolidate, or replace over the next five years, and what should replace them. The relative advantages of a traditional managed-services model versus a platform-first operating model built around standardized, reusable capabilities, self-service, automation, common engineering patterns, and measurable product or mission outcomes. How VA should sustain mission-critical services during modernization while improving availability, recovery, resilience, observability, security, maintainability, and interoperability. How VA can scale to future enterprise demand without relying primarily on open-ended labor or team augmentation, including ways to classify complexity, size work, and introduce new in-scope capabilities consistently. How commercial and performance models should evolve as automation increases, including how VA should measure value, validate productivity and cost reductions, and avoid incentives that reward activity or consumption rather than outcomes. How VA should preserve portability, Government access to technical assets and data, and the ability to transition products and services without dependence on proprietary contractor-controlled tooling. Current Environment and Working Assumptions For purposes of responding to this RFI, respondents may assume that MOSAIC could include some combination of continuous data-quality assessment and improvement, multi-modal data access and delivery (transactional, bulk/analytical, event-driven, and AI-ready data products), data sharing and integration, sustainment and operational support, modernization, data landscape assessment and roadmap planning, and transition activities for a defined initial product set, with the potential for additional in-scope enterprise demand over time. Respondents should not assume that current architecture, tools, licenses, organizational boundaries, or delivery practices will remain unchanged. Where a recommendation depends on a particular Government-furnished platform, commercial product, licensing model, authoritative data source, or separately managed enterprise service, identify that dependency and explain why it matters. What VA Is Asking Industry to Address VA requests candid, experience-based responses focused on the future state VA should pursue, and the practical decisions required to achieve it. Responses should distinguish between current demonstrated capabilities and future roadmap capabilities and should identify material assumptions, dependencies, risks, transition considerations, and conditions necessary for success. VA seeks recommendations that will improve the quality, reliability, and reusability of its authoritative data and make that data readily consumable through multiple access modes, including AI-enabled uses. Recommendations should also address how VA can simplify the environment, increase reuse and interoperability, reduce technical debt and avoidable operating costs, and improve resilience and security. VA is particularly interested in durable enterprise capabilities rather than approaches that preserve existing structures for their own sake. This RFI is issued solely for information gathering and acquisition planning purposes and is intended to support the Department of Veterans Affairs' market research and ongoing refinement of requirements, acquisition strategy, contract scope, sequencing, and commercial structure. This RFI is not a solicitation and does not constitute an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation, or Request for Proposal. The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation, award

The contractor must report any outliers identified during testing within 24 hours of receiving laboratory results. Completes follow-up testing as ordered by engineering for out-of-range water parameters per the ST108:2023 and VHA water contract/SOW. The contractor shall provide VA end users with access to web-based reporting software for ongoing review of water testing data, historical trends, and compliance documentation. All reports must clearly highlight or delineate outliers and be designed to provide ease of reading, ensuring information is presented in a clear, organized, and actionable format. Contractor shall provide consultative services as needed, such as resolving abnormal water testing results, water system analysis, and mitigation of test results. title: Military Plans Specialist Support Services
description: 2. REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION & Performance duties 2.1 Scope of Support The Contractor shall provide operational and strategic planning advisory support to the Area Support Group-Jordan (ASG-J) Operations Directorate (S-3), assisting in the coordination, development, and execution of comprehensive operational plans, contingency plans, exercises, and force protection programs in support of United States Army Central (USARCENT) and adjacent USCENTCOM entities. 2.2 Core Responsibilities and Duty Allocation The following major duties (percentages approximate effort allocation) are derived from the official Army Position Description: Physical Security and Force Protection Planning (approx. 30%): Develop, implement, review, and update comprehensive physical security and force protection plans, policies, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Assist the ASG-J Provost Marshal Office (PMO) in identifying vulnerabilities and performing technical force protection inspections, assessments, and surveys. Coordinate Mission Assurance Assessments (MAA) with USARCENT, conduct associated In-Progress Reviews (IPRs) and briefings and develop corrective action plans for identified deficiencies. Coordinate with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) to conduct physical security/force protection reviews on installation master plans, construction projects, and facility renovations pursuant to applicable DoD and Army regulations. Deliberate and Crisis Action Planning / Contingency Plans (approx. 30%): Integrate deliberate and crisis action planning support across USARCENT, subordinate formations, and USCENTCOM. Serve as technical lead and project coordinator for contingency planning efforts, contributing directly to the drafting and refinement of Operations Plans (OPLANs), Concept Plans (CONPLANs), Operations Orders (OPORDs), Fragmentary Orders (FRAGOs), and Functional Plans. Utilize the Joint Operation Planning and Execution System (JOPES) / Adaptive Planning and Execution (APEX) enterprise to formulate cyber operations annexes, appendices, and operational deployment workflows for deployed forces. Exercise and Training Support / MDMP-JOPP (approx. 20%): Support ASG-J S-3 operations to ensure field and command-post exercises align with USARCENT doctrine, policies, and priorities. Apply deep operational understanding of Commander�s Intent, Running Estimates, Intelligence Preparation of the Battlefield (IPB), Deliberate Planning, and the Military Decision Making Process (MDMP) / Joint Operational Planning Process (JOPP) across Unified, Joint, Combined, and Service-component echelons. Facilitate Operational Planning Teams (OPTs) and Joint Planning Groups (JPGs); conduct Course of Action (COA) development, analysis (wargaming), comparison, and decision briefing preparation for senior leadership. Inter-Agency Representation and Staff Coordination (approx. 20%): Represent the ASG-J S-3 during cross-functional working groups, operational syncs, and planning conferences. Liaise with internal directorates, tenant units, host-nation representatives, and higher headquarters to align ASG-J operational roadmaps with theater campaign goals. 2.3 Mandatory Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) Comprehensive proficiency in Army regulations and doctrine pertaining to Base Operations Support-Integrator (BOS-I), Common-User Logistics/Base Operations (COM-I), Physical Security, and Force Protection. Working knowledge of DoD directives, relevant U.S. statutes, and bilateral frameworks, including the U.S.�Jordanian Defense Cooperation Agreement (DCA). Familiarity with USARCENT, 1st Theater Sustainment Command (1TSC), and USCENTCOM operational architecture and associated OPLANs/CONPLANs. Working knowledge of Theater Provided Equipment (TPE), Modified Table of Organization and Equipment (MTOE), and Tables of Distribution and Allowances (TDA) structures. Exceptional written and verbal military communication skills, including experience authoring formal executive summaries, military orders, and general officer-level briefings. 3. Deployability & Travel: Contractor personnel must be deployable and eligible for overseas travel. Business travel (Temporary Duty - TDY) within the USCENTCOM Area of Responsibility (Jordan and adjacent Middle Eastern countries) is anticipated up to 20% of annual performance. Medical & Theater Entry Requirements: Contractor personnel must meet all CENTCOM Mod/theater-specific medical clearance standards, including required immunization profiles (e.g., seasonal influenza and applicable DoD overseas health mandates) and Synchronized Predeployment and Operational Tracker (SPOT) / Letter of Authorization (LOA) processing. title: High Voltage Power Supplies (HVPS) for Electronic Fish Barriers
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Chicago District, is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement of six high voltage power supplies (HVPS) for Barriers IIA and IIB near Romeoville, Illinois. The intention is to procure this requirement on a competitive basis.*************BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES (IN FULL OR IN PART) OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION, and multiple awards MAY be made. USACE is conducting market research to determine whether a small business set-aside is achievable under the newly restructured terms, or whether it will proceed under full and open competition with subcontracting opportunities. We recently solicited unrestricted but had a bid bust, so are restructuring our requirement with the elimination of storage requirements. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions.*************DISCLAIMER*************THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ANY ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT.*************PROGRAM BACKGROUND: The HPVS support Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal Electric Dispersal Barrier System, barriers IIA and IIB. These Electric Dispersal Barriers protect the Great Lakes from the invasive species.*************REQUIRED CAPABILITIES*************The Contractor shall provide engineering and site verification; design submittals; fabrication; factory acceptance testing (FAT); operator and maintenance training during or immediately after FAT; technical documentation; packaging, transportation, delivery and unloading; and warranty coverage services in support of the areas specified in Program Background (above). Further details: a) Four 1.5 megawatt (MW) high voltage power supplies for Pulser 1 and Pulser 2 at Barriers IIA and IIB. and b) Two 350 kilowatt (kW) high voltage power supplies for Pulser 3 at Barriers IIA and IIB.*************Technical capability overview*************The replacement equipment will support existing pulse generating units and capacitor banks serving the electric dispersal barriers. The following summarizes the anticipated requirement for market research; it is not a complete fabrication specification.*************Input power: 480 volts AC, three-phase, 60 hertz.*************Output ratings: each 1.5 MW unit to provide 2,000 volts DC at 750 amperes and 2,200 volts DC at approximately 682 amperes, subject to its 1.5 MW continuous power limit. Each 350 kW unit to provide up to 1,000 volts DC at 350 amperes.*************Power conversion: copper-wound transformers and a 24-pulse silicon controlled rectifier (SCR) configuration, or an equivalent approach for Government consideration that achieves the required performance and harmonic reduction.*************Integration: compatibility with existing equipment spaces, access routes, electrical connections, cooling systems, and the Pulse Generating Control System. Identify any necessary changes to existing equipment or interfaces rather than assuming they are included in this procurement.*************Controls and safety: local and remote monitoring, communications, alarms, protective devices, and interlocks compatible with facility requirements. Existing interfaces include DeviceNet; the draft SOW also addresses Modbus TCP/IP.*************Operating conditions: continuous barrier service, compatibility with the pulsed load and existing capacitor banks, and the draft SOW ambient range of 0 to 50 degrees Celsius and up to 95 percent non-condensing relative humidity.*************Cooling and handling: demonstrate feasible heat rejection within available site cooling capacity and identify equipment dimensions, weights, lifting provisions, shipping configuration, and delivery/unloading needs. Early design submittals would establish dimensions, weights, anchorage, power and control connections, communications, cooling requirements, and heat loads in sufficient detail for USACE to develop the separate installation design while fabrication proceeds. Final deliverables would include drawings of the equipment as fabricated, Operation and Maintenance manuals, test reports, training materials, and storage/preservation instructions.***************************************If your organization has the potential capacity to perform this requirement, please provide the following information*************1) Organization name, address, email address, UEI and cage code, Web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization, and *************2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. Submit concise responses in the same organized format as below. Identify assumptions and distinguish firm capabilities from proposed alternatives. Partial responses from manufacturers or prospective subcontractors are welcome; clearly identify which portions your firm can support.**************************I. Interest and role Would your firm pursue this revised requirement as a prime contractor, manufacturer supplying a prime, distributor/integrator, or team member? Identify the intended manufacturer and major work allocations, if known. Explain any barriers to submitting an offer, including whether your response depends on finding a teaming partner.*************II. Relevant capability Provide up to three examples of comparable industrial HVPS or rectifier projects, including power/voltage ratings, application, approximate completion date, and your role. Describe experience with pulsed loads, copper-wound transformers, harmonic reduction, controls integration, and liquid cooling. *************III. Technical feasibility Identify requirements that would prevent participation, materially increase cost or lead time, or require an exception. Address the 24-pulse approach or proposed equivalent, output ratings, ambient conditions, cooling capacity and water quality, controls/protocol compatibility, physical fit, and any facility modifications. Describe the specific clarification or performance-based alternative recommended.*************Factory testing and training Describe available test facilities and a practical FAT approach for both ratings. Manufacturing and FAT would occur at the contractor/manufacturer facility. Distinguish full-power tests from separate full-voltage/full-current tests or simulations, and identify limitations in reproducing the installed pulsed load. Recommend measurable acceptance criteria and the equipment or site data needed. Confirm ability to train Government personnel during or immediately after FAT.*************IV. description: Prodloužení technické podpory / maintenance dodaných produktů s platností min. do 10/2027, které bude poskytované jednotlivými výrobci v rozsahu a v souladu se zadávacími podmínkami. Zadavatel v roce 2019 pořídil v rámci projektu „Bezpečnost informačních systémů PNO“ produkty uvedené v „příloze č. 1 – cenová nabídka – prodloužení licencí“, kterým končí technická podpora / maintenance poskytovaná výrobcem. Zadavatel požaduje nacenit prodloužení technické podpory / maintenance dodaných produktů s platností min. do 10/2027, které bude poskytované jednotlivými výrobci (čestné prohlášení uchazeče není akceptováno). Uchazeč doplní ceny jednotlivých položek uvedených v Příloze č. 1 – cenová nabídka – prodloužení licencí, která bude nedílnou součástí návrhu smlouvy. Bližší podrobnosti v zadávací dokumentaci a jejich přílohách.

PSC Code: Z2AA NAICS Code: 236220 Small Business Size Standard: $45M Description: This is a Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract that provides for an indefinite quantity of supplies or services during a fixed period. The GSA intends to award multiple contracts for General Construction Services. After award of the IDIQ all awardees will be provided fair opportunity in accordance with FAR 16.507-2 for discrete construction projects where a single task order will be issued based on selection criteria established at the ordering level, unless an exemption exists in accordance with FAR 16.507-6. The General Contractor (GC) shall serve as the single point of responsibility and must supervise, administer, coordinate, perform, and contract all management, labor, materials, equipment, and construction activities required to successfully execute each assigned project. Construction services will be required to be performed at federally owned and leased locations. The operational scope encompasses comprehensive general construction, repair, alteration, and modernization services for existing real property facilities. The General Contractor (GC) shall supervise, administer, perform, and contract all construction activities required to complete a project. Construction services include, but are not limited to office construction and/or renovations/repairs, office space renovations, MEP (Mechanical/Electrical/Plumbing) repairs/modifications/replacement, fire sprinkler systems repairs/modification/replacement, sitework, exterior construction repair and alterations (including facades and roofs), demolition (including abatement of hazardous materials), elevator modernizations, work in technically sensitive environments like laboratories, SCIF�s etc., work in high-security data centers and critical infrastructure control systems, construction work in high security buildings, as well as any other general construction activities. The scope will include design-build services. The GC may be required to utilize the following delivery methods to deliver projects for the GSA: 1. Design/Bid/Build (DBB) Traditional 2. Design/Build (D/B) The primary geography will cover: -All of Washington, D.C. -Virginia: Arlington County, Fairfax County, Loudon County, Independent Cities of Alexandria, Fairfax, and Falls Church -Maryland: Montgomery County, Prince George's County The Government may unilaterally expand the geography to cover any additional counties in the states of Maryland and Virginia. GSA reserves the right to expand, within scope, the geographic areas covered by the awarded contracts by bilateral agreement with any or all contract holders based on agency needs and requirements. The Maximum Ordering Limit (MOL) for this contract vehicle is $500,000,000.00. Meaning the cumulative total for all task orders awarded to all contractors over the life of the contract (5 Years) is not anticipated to exceed $500,000,000.00. There is no MOL per contractor or per performance period. The general task order range will be between $350,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. There will be a base period of one (1) year, and there will be four (4) option periods of one-year each, for a total possible performance period of five (5) years. The government intends to award approximately eighteen (18) contracts, inclusive of a target of twelve (12) contract reserves. However, the Government reserves the right to make more, fewer, or no awards, depending on the results of the evaluation, availability of funding, and the Government�s needs. The government is reserving three (3) contracts each for the following socioeconomic designations: 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB, for a target of twelve (12) contract reserves. However, the Government reserves the right to make more, fewer, or no reserve awards, depending on the results of the evaluation, availability of funding, and the Government�s needs. Award Methodology This solicitation will be executed pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.103-3 (RFO-2025-15), Highest technically rated with a fair and reasonable price approach. Pursuant to FAR Clause 52.215-1 Instructions to Offerors-Competitive Acquisition, and FAR 15.203 (RFO-2025-15), the Government intends to evaluate proposals and make competitive awards without negotiations with offerors although it reserves the right to negotiate should it be determined to be necessary. Competitive proposals shall be evaluated and assessed based on the factors specified in this solicitation. For this solicitation, all evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, are significantly more important than price. The Technical Evaluation Factors will be: Prior Experience Past Performance Evidence of Bonding Capacity: Go/No Go. title: Request for Information for On-Site Fabrication and Assembly of a Three-Bay High-Performance Magazine (HPM) Structure
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY AND YOUR RESPONSE IS NOT AN OFFER. SERIOUS INQUIRIES ONLY AND SUBMISSIONS MUST BE FROM A US-BASED CONTRACTOR. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTES (RFQ). NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION DOES NOT COMMIT THE GOVERNMENT TO PAY ANY COSTS INCURRED IN PREPARATION OF ANY SUBMISSION TO THIS NOTICE, OR TO CONTRACT FOR ITEMS/SERVICES. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses to the RFI will not be returned. Information provided in response to this RFI will be used to assess tradeoffs and alternatives available for determining how to proceed in the acquisition process for a solution. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c)(2), responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) is conducting market research to determine sources� competencies and capabilities to execute the on-site fabrication and final assembly of a three-bay, monolithic reinforced concrete High-Performance Magazine (HPM) structure. This is for a test structure for experimental purposes only and in the course of testing the structure will be completely destroyed and the site will be retrograded. The scope requires the full, in-situ assembly of the HPM structure at a designated Government test range at Fort Polk, LA. The process involves mobilizing all materials and equipment to the site, erecting temporary formwork systems, installing reinforcing steel cages, and placing concrete to form the final test structure according to the attached Description of Requirement (DOR). This is not a pre-cast or modular system; the final deliverable is the fully assembled and cured structure fabricated at its final location. The primary materials to be procured and processes to be performed are listed below. Reinforcing Steel (Rebar): Procure, deliver, and install prefabricated steel reinforcement into a intergrated cage within the formwork Cast-in-Place Concrete: Procure and received ready-mix concrete; place material into the erected formwork; perform consolidation, finishing and curing. Structural Sand Fill: Procure, deliver, and install sand into desiginated wall cavities post-concrete. Concrete Formwork: Fabricate or procure formwork panels; perform on-site erection, bracing, and subsequent stripping of the complete system for walls, slabs, and doors. Reinforced Concrete Doors: Perform on-site formwork erection, rebar installation, and concrete placement for three separate door components. Embedded Items: Procure and install all required embeds, sleeves, and plates within the formwork prior to concrete placement. A DRAFT Description of Requirement (DOR), which includes a detailed description of the structure, is attached. Please note this is subject to change. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to obtain information on the availability and capability of vendors to procure the necessary raw materials, provide shipping of materials and equipment to Fort Polk, LA, and perform the complete on-site fabrication and assembly of the structure to specification. Additionally, this RFI seeks to determine industry interest in participation for market research purposes before a Request for Quote (RFQ) is released for these requirements. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFQ or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Respondents are requested to review the attached DRAFT DOR and submit responses to the following questions: 1. Contact information: Interested organizations should respond by providing the Government the following information: Company name, Address, Point of Contact, business title, Telephone number, Email address, Company Cage Code, Primary NAICS, Business Size, i.e., Large, Small (if small, state your category). Current Registration in SAM, Webpage address. 2. Capabilities Statement: A description of capabilities in providing 1) the minimum required items and capabilities described in the RFI and Draft DOR to the specified location(s) and 2) Experience. Previous procurement information, including contract numbers and customers, is recommended. 3. Business Status (based on NAICS 238120): Please indicate the business status of your company (Socio-Economic Factors: 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Business, Small Disadvantaged Business etc.). 4. Answer the following Questions: All interested contractors are requested to provide comprehensive written responses to the questions below. Question #1- Project Experience: Provide at least two (2) and no more than four (4) examples of projects completed by your company within the last 7 years that are of a similar scale and complexity to the HPM structure. For each project, provide the following details: Project Name and a brief description. Final concrete compressive strength(s) and total cubic yards placed. Approximate final reinforcing steel density (lbs/CY). A summary of your company's role (e.g., Prime Contractor, Concrete Subcontractor). Question #2- Self-Consolidating Concrete (SCC) Experience: The requirement is for 10,000 PSI SCC. Describe your company's experience with high-strength SCC. Specify your approach to: Mix design submittal and verification. Managing the high fluid pressure of SCC on formwork systems. On-site Quality Control testing Question #3- Formwork Systems: This project requires a robust, engineered formwork system. Does your company have in-house engineering capability to design and develop formwork plans, or is this service subcontracted? Please describe a challenging formwork scenario your company has successfully managed on a past project. Question #4- Reinforcing Steel: The project specifications require continuous, non-spliced rebar in many areas. Describe your company's experience and methods for installing long, heavy, and continuous reinforcing steel in congested, multi-layered wall and slab assemblies. Question #5- Core Competencies (Self-Perform vs. Subcontract): Please indicate which of the following core activities your company typically self-performs versus subcontracts: Heavy Concrete Formwork Design and Erection Reinforcing Steel Installation Concrete Placement and Finishing Earthwork and Site Logistics Materials QC Testing Question #6- Overall Capability: After reviewing the Description of Requirement, does your company have the capability to procure all materials and fully execute the on-site fabrication and assembly of the HPM structure as specified? If not, please specify which items or processes cannot be provided and why. Interested vendors must provide the above information no later than 3:00 PM Central Standard Time (CST) on 04 November 2026. Responses must be emailed to Shinita Jordan at Shinita.M.Jordan@usace.army.mil AND Sonia Boyd at Sonia.J.Boyd@usace.army.mil. Any questions related to this notice must be submitted in writing to Shinita Jordan and Sonia Boyd. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. The Government will not reimburse companies for any costs associated with the submissions of their responses.

title: Germany – Fire-alarm system installation work – Modernisierung GS Dorschbergschule - Gefahrenmelde- und Alarmanlage
description: Die Grundschule Dorschberg in Wörth a. Rh. wurde 1966 baulich errichtet und liegt hinter dem Mittelbau der Carl–Benz–Gesamtschule in Wörth am Rhein. Die Grundschule besteht aus vier Gebäudeteilen, zu welchen ein ein- bzw. zweigeschossiger Gebäudeteil mit Verbindungsgängen gehört sowie eine Pausenhalle mit einem Verwaltungstrakt und einem eingeschossigen Pavillonbau mit vier Pavillongebäuden. Die Gebäude sind mit Pausengängen verbunden und verfügen über zwei Toilettengebäude. Die ein- bis zweigeschossigen Gebäude wurden in massiver Bauweise mit Beton-Fertigteilen errichtet und weisen Flachdächer in unterschiedlichen Höhenlagen mit umlaufender Attika auf und wurden bis heute mehrfach saniert und modernisiert. Mitte der 1990er Jahre fand eine Betonsanierung statt. In diesem Zuge wurde ein Wärmedämm-Verbundsystem und die Alucobond-Verkleidungen der Attiken und der Fertigteilstützen angebracht. Wesentliche bauliche Maßnahmen - Der bestehende eingeschossige Klassentrakt wird aufgestockt und der bisherige Innenhofbereich zwischen den beiden bestehenden Klassentrakten wird geschlossen und überdacht. Hierzu wird die nicht ausreichend tragfähige Spannbetondecke über dem nördlichen Klassentakt zurück gebaut und durch eine neue Stahlbeton-Massivdecke ersetzt. - Das neue Obergeschoss wird in vorgefertigter Holzbauweise mit tragenden Wänden als Massivholzkonstruktion bzw. Holzständerkonstruktion und oberster Geschossdecke als Brettsperrholzkonstruktion errichtet. - Die zentrale Aula wird mit einer Glasdachkonstruktion versehen. - Die Spannbetondecke im Flurbereich über dem bestehenden Kriechkeller des Nordtraktes muss durch Stahlträger ertüchtigt werden. - Kleinteilige Grundrissänderungen im Bestand - Die Pavillons werden entkernt und zur erweiterten überdachten Pausenhoffläche - Verbesserung des Wärmeschutzes sämtlicher Gebäudehüllflächen (Dachflächen, Fenster, hinterlüftete Holzfassaden, Kellerdeckendämmung) - Modernisierung der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung inkl. kontrollierten Lüftungseinrichtung mit Wärmerückgewinnung, energiesparender Beleuchtungssysteme, Gebäudeautomation, einschließlich der digitalen Anforderungen an Schulgebäude - Optimierung des Brandschutzes und Umsetzung des schulischen Schutzkonzepts

title: Bulgaria – Dam construction work – Увеличаване на обема на долния изравнител на ПАВЕЦ „Чаира“ с изграждане на язовир „Яденица“ и реверсивен напорен тунел за връзка с язовир „Чаира“, реф. № 26ИП-Р19А101
description: Предметът на обществената поръчка включва изпълнение на строително-монтажни работи и изготвяне на екзекутивна документация за обект: „Увеличаване на обема на долния изравнител на ПАВЕЦ „Чаира“ с изграждане на язовир „Яденица“ и реверсивен напорен тунел за връзка с язовир „Чаира“. Основни подобекти на проекта са: • Язовирна стена и прилежащи съоръжения в т. ч. Инжекционна галерия; Шахтов преливник с отводяща галерия, бързоток и енергогасител; Основен изпускател; Контролно измервателна система; Малка ВЕЦ на екологични води; Насип за укрепване на брега на язовирното езеро в зоната на Яденишки разлом; Укрепване на свлачище в района на временния взривен склад на площадка „Яденица“; Противоерозионна защита на ската над енергогасителя на язовирната стена до пътя за връзка с короната на стената; Противоерозионна защита на изкопни откоси на експлоатационен път по левия бряг на р. Яденица, участък от km 4+860 до km 5+770; Корекция на р. Яденица след язовирната стена; Присъединяване на постоянните съоръжения (потребители) към районна мрежа 20 kV в периода на експлоатация и резервни захранвания; • Реверсивен напорен тунел и прилежащи съоръжения с подобекти: Реверсивен напорен тунел; Входно съоръжение „Яденица“; Савачна шахта „Яденица“, Савачна шахта „Чаира“; Системи за пълнене и изпразване на тунела с апаратна камера и тунела за достъп до апаратна камера; Прозорец за достъп до реверсивен напорен тунел; Изместване на водопровод за ПАВЕЦ „Чаира“ от Манавско дере; • Експлоатационни пътища; • Обслужваща сграда; Система за физическа защита. Изпълнението на поръчката ще се извърши съгласно изготвен и одобрен от Възложителя и от Министерство на регионалното развитие и благоустройство работен проект, техническата спецификация, вкл. допълнителни технически изисквания на Възложителя за поръчката. Работният проект за изпълнението на обекта, с допълнителни указания относно ценообразуването и техническите изисквания ще бъдат предоставени с поканата за участие на допуснатите кандидати - за изготвяне на оферта.

title: Sweden – Operation of a sewage plant – Hyresupphandling av pilotanläggning för vattenåtervinning
description: Kalmar Vatten AB (KVAB) bjuder in leverantörer att delta i en spännande och framtidsinriktad upphandling med fokus på att utveckla nya lösningar för en trygg och hållbar dricksvattenförsörjning. Mot bakgrund av framtida utmaningar med minskad tillgång till råvatten avser KVAB att hyra en pilotanläggning för avancerad vattenrening under en period om två år. Anläggningen ska placeras vid det nybyggda Kalmarsundsverket i Kalmar och användas för att undersöka möjligheterna att återvinna renat avloppsvatten till dricksvattenkvalitet. Pilotanläggningen ska omfatta flera avancerade reningssteg, såsom ozonering, omvänd osmos m.fl. Projektet genomförs med stöd av Tillväxtverket och Region Kalmar län.

Our strategy is a for five to ten-year cost plus fixed-fee contract (basic plus four to nine option years) and will potentially continue through FY37. title: Y--AK FWS AK PEN NWR REPLACE COLD STRG 5
description: This is a Synopsis/Pre-Solicitation Notice. The final solicitation package will follow. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) anticipates soliciting proposals for the demolition of an existing cold storage building and the design and construction of a new detached cold storage facility at the Alaska Peninsula/Becharof National Wildlife Refuge in King Salmon, Alaska. This project is supported by the Great American Outdoor Act (GAOA) Summary: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service anticipates awarding a single firm-fixed-price design-build construction contract for the demolition of the existing cold storage building and the design and construction of a new detached cold storage facility of approximately 5,500 to 5,800 square feet. The project is located in a remote area of King Salmon, Alaska. The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, tools, supplies, transportation, shipping, handling, logistics support, and incidentals necessary to complete the work. The contractor shall be responsible for all transportation and delivery requirements associated with furnishing materials and equipment to the project site. Acquisition Information NAICS Code: 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside pursuant to FAR 19.502-2 Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price This acquisition will be conducted in accordance with: FAR Part 36, Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts; and FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. In accordance with FAR 36.204(f), the estimated magnitude of construction for this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. Detailed project requirements and specifications will be provided in the solicitation upon issuance. Source Selection Method The procurement will utilize: FAR Part 36.3, Two-Phase Design-Build Selection Procedures; and FAR Part 15, Best-Value Tradeoff Process. The Government intends to award one contract to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government using the tradeoff process described in FAR 15.101-1. The evaluation factors are anticipated to be: Experience and Technical Capability Past Performance Price The relative importance of the evaluation factors will be identified in the solicitation System for Award Management (SAM) Offerors must be actively registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be eligible for award. Information regarding SAM registration is available at http://www.sam.gov. Payments will be made via Electronic Funds Transfer using information contained within the contractor's SAM registration.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Post-delivery support of developed?space and ground hardware and software
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE General Information Notice Type:?Special Notice Contracting Office:?Space RCO Title:?Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Post-delivery support of developed?space and ground hardware and software. Response Date:?No later than 1500 MST on 04 NOV 2026 NAICS Code:?541715 Product Service Code (PSC):?DA10 Description: The Space Rapid Capabilities Office (Space RCO) intends to solicit and negotiate a contract on a sole-source basis with?Systems & Technology Research, LLC, Woburn, Massachusetts?under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Requirement Description: Space RCO requires?post-delivery support of developed space and ground hardware and software. This effort will continue to provide systems engineering support for verification and validation of interface requirements, hardware integration and test, and on-orbit troubleshooting as the payloads are integrated onto host vehicles, tested, launched, and perform on-orbit. The instant action is to procure services to transition a prototype ground system to a full operational capability. The requirements outline a need for software development and integration expertise to enhance the existing system with a new graphical user interface (GUI), integrate mission-unique software (MUS), improve telemetry processing and data handling, and ensure the system can support long-term, 24/7 operations. The effort also requires integration with the R2C2 Acme Ground Segment, maintaining external connections, development on cloud infrastructure, and adherence to cybersecurity and systems engineering best practices. Full operational capability should be obtained within 6 months from ATP. Projected Base and Option Year CLIN Structure: CLIN 0001 (CPFF) - 2-Year Base, 3 (three) 1-Year Options. CLINs 0003, 0004 (Cost Only, No Fee) - 2-Year Base, 3 (three) 1-Year Options. CLIN 0002 (T&M) - 1-Year Base, 4 (four) 1-Year Options. Reason for Sole Source: Systems & Technology Research, LLC is the original developer of the prototype ground system. The contractor holds specialized technical expertise and existing infrastructure knowledge required to transition this system to Full Operational Capability (FOC). No other source possesses the requisite technical familiarity to meet the aggressive 6-month FOC requirement without causing unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency's critical requirements and generating substantial duplication of costs that is not expected to be recovered through competition. Submission Details: This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. To be considered viable, any response must explicitly demonstrate the vendor's technical capability to: Achieve FOC of the specific prototype ground system within six (6) months of ATP. Perform direct, proven integration with the R2C2 Acme Ground Segment without reliance on Systems & Technology Research, LLC proprietary data. Execute the required cloud infrastructure development and 24/7 telemetry processing capabilities. (Generic marketing materials will not be evaluated.) Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Responses must be received no later than 1500 MST on 04 NOV 2026. Responses must be submitted via email to Monica Torrez at monica.torrez.1.ctr@spaceforce.mil and Mariacheska Legendre at mariacheska.legendre@spaceforce.mil.

title: Denmark – Financial and insurance services – Udbud af delkontrakter vedrørende administration af selvforsikringsordninger
description: Forsvaret (herefter benævnt ”FMI”) er som statslig myndighed selvforsikrer, jf. cirkulære om selvforsikring i staten mv. (CIR nr. 9783 af 9. december 2005). Forsvaret har som følge heraf vedtaget interne forsikringsbetingelser, der blandt andet omfatter Forsvarets udsendte medarbejdere. Den udbudte opgave under Delkontrakt 1 omfatter administration af Forsvarets selvforsikringsordning, herunder behandling og udbetaling af refusion af skadeanmeldelser fra hele verden, der er relateret til: - Sygdom og hjemtransport - Kollektiv heltidsulykkesdækning. Opgaven omfatter også at stille en døgnbemandet alarmcentral til rådighed, der skal sikre behandling og opfølgning ved akut opståede skader og sygdom, der er omfattet af forsikringsbetingelserne. Den udbudte opgave under Delkontrakt 2 omfatter administration af Forsvarets selvforsikringsordning, herunder behandling og udbetaling af refusion af skadeanmeldelser fra hele verden, der er relateret til: - Transportskade på bohave (flyttegods ifm. udstationering, hjemkaldelse eller forflyttelse af udsendte til lokationer udenfor Danmark) - Skader i forbindelse med opmagasinering af bohave, og - Katastrofedækning. Det er den/de kommende leverandør/leverandører på delkontrakterne, der skal varetage og behandle henvendelser vedrørende skader fra den sikrede personkreds samt foretage refusion af udgifter på Forsvarets vegne. Forsikringsadministrationsordningen for hver af delkontrakterne skal udføres i henhold til de af Forsvaret opstillede betingelser, summer, dækninger og vilkår.

buyer: Office fédéral des constructions et de la logistique OFCL
title: (b26055-3) Berne, Monbijoustr. 40, rénovation totale / CFC 230
description:
L'Office fédéral des constructions et de la logistique (OFCL) a commandé la rénovation totale du bâtiment situé au 40, Monbijoustrasse, à Berne. Cet édifice remarquable se compose de deux corps de bâtiment : un bâtiment de tête et une aile latérale.

Pendant la rénovation du bâtiment, les postes de travail seront transférés dans un site de relogement. Le bâtiment restera inoccupé pendant la durée des travaux. À l’avenir, il sera utilisé par l’administration fédérale et comme établissement de formation (bâtiment de tête) pour la Haute école fédérale en formation professionnelle (HEFP).

Le bâtiment administratif (ancienne Direction générale des douanes) situé au 40, Monbijoustrasse est l’un des édifices les plus emblématiques et les plus remarquables du modernisme d’après-guerre des années 1950 à Berne. Le bien est classé dans l’inventaire des bâtiments comme objet K digne de protection, fait partie d’une zone ISOS d’importance nationale (A) et figure dans l’inventaire de protection des biens culturels en tant qu’objet d’importance nationale. En conséquence, il est soumis à des exigences accrues en matière de conservation du patrimoine et sa rénovation totale est réalisée en concertation avec le service de conservation du patrimoine de la ville de Berne.

Le 3e étage de l’aile latérale doit répondre à des exigences particulièrement strictes de la conservation des monuments historiques, en raison de l’obligation de le garder dans son état historique d’origine en tant qu’étage de direction.

Au 4e trimestre 2026, des « travaux anticipés 2026 » seront réalisés.

Il inclut la responsabilité globale (gestion) des livraisons et des montages effectués par les sous-traitants pour les cahiers des charges / lots suivants :

  • Lot 3 : distribution électrique principale
  • Lot 4 : système d'éclairage de secours, y compris les luminaires de sécurité
  • Lot 5 : luminaires techniques et sources lumineuses

title: Luxembourg – Computer-related services – Call for Tenders for the selection of Artificial Intelligence Gigafactory Consortia and the establishment of AI Gigafactories
description: The overall objective of this Call is the selection of Artificial Intelligence Gigafactory (AIGF) Consortia, which will establish and operate the AIGFs and from which the Contracting Parties will acquire AI compute access time. More in detail, the specific objectives of this Call are as follows: - Selection of AIGF Consortia: Following a rigorous evaluation of the tenders by the EuroHPC JU with the support of independent experts, the Governing Board will make an award decision, establishing a ranked list of successful AIGF Consortia. - Procurement of Compute Access Time: To establish a framework for the joint acquisition of a guaranteed share of AI compute access time from the selected AIGF Consortia, formalised through the signature of a Framework Contract and a number of subsequent Specific Contracts with the successful AIGF Consortia. AIGF refers to state-of-the-art large-scale facility with sufficient capacity to handle the complete lifecycle, from development to large-scale inference, of very large AI models and applications, providing a supercomputing service infrastructure which is composed of AI-optimised computing capacity, a supporting data centre infrastructure including high-capacity storage and networking, dedicated secure cloud user access environments, and specialised secure AI-oriented support services for its advanced operations, all of which are supported by an environmentally sustainable infrastructure, in particular for energy and water supply systems.

description: Der Planfeststellungsbeschluss für die Herstellung des Hochwasserschutzes (HWS) der Ortslage Herzberg (Elster) Teilobjekt 1 liegt seit August 2023 vor. Auf der linken Seite der Schwarzen Elster wurden seit 2024 die Bauabschnitte 1 und 4 fertiggestellt. Derzeit werden die Bauabschnitte 2 und 3 bis Ende 2027 umgesetzt. Ab Oktober 2026 werden auf der rechten Seite die Abschnitte 1 bis 3 "BA1-3re" über 2 Jahre begonnen. Die Baukosten sind mit ca. 5 Mio. EUR veranschlagt. Die Hochwasserschutzanlage wird größtenteils als freistehende Spundwand realisiert. In kürzeren Bereichen ist die Spundwand überdeckt bzw. wird ein DIN-gerechter Erddeich errichtet. Gemäß Vorgaben der Planfeststellung sind die Baumaßnahmen durch eine ökologische Bauüberwachung (= Umweltbaubegleitung UBB) zu begleiten. Die UBB soll mit dieser Vergabe vertraglich gebunden werden. Inhalt der Leistung sind die Überwachung der Durchführung der im Landschaftspflegerischen Begleitplan (LBP) festgelegten Schutz-, Vermeidungs- und trassennahen Kompensationsmaßnahmen. Die Überwachung eingriffsferner Kompensationsmaßnahmen nach § 39 HOAI sind nicht Bestandteil dieser Vergabe. Diese Maßnahmen wurden ab Anfang 2022 umgesetzt und befinden sich bis Ende 2026 in der Entwicklungs-, anschließend in der Unterhaltungspflege.

description: Die Kreisstadt Homburg plant die touristische Neuerschließung des Schlossberges. Jahrhundert und den Schlossberghöhlen mit beeindruckenden Kuppeln und Stollengängen. Sie gelten als "die größten Buntsandsteinhöhlen Europas". Beide Anlagen sind denkmalrechtlich geschützt, die Schlossberghöhlen befinden sich darüber hinaus zusätzlich unter bergrechtlicher Aufsicht. Das Gesamtprojekt ist in zwei Teilprojekte unterteilt. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung ist im Rahmen des TP 1 die Untertageausbauplanung - neues Höhleneingangsbauwerk - neue Felsenkammern im Luftschacht - neue Felsenkammer als Einstiegsbereich am neuen Höhlenaufzug - bergmännischer Ausbau.

title: Germany – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Einführung von Ki in der Eingangsverarbeitung
description: Gegenstand des Verfahrens: Der Beitragsservice von ARD, ZDF und Deutschlandradio beschafft einen KI-basierten Service zur automatisierten Verarbeitung eingehender schriftlicher Sendungen (Papier/Scan, E-Mail, Fax), der als Managed Service (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS) auf einer souveränen Cloud betrieben werden soll. Der KI-Service klassifiziert die Sendungen nach der Dokumentart-Systematik des Beitragsservice (DAK/SDAK), erkennt das fachliche Anliegen und extrahiert die für die Weiterverarbeitung erforderlichen Fachdaten. Die Ergebnisse werden jeweils mit einem Confidence-Score als strukturierte JSON-Objekte an den bestehenden Verarbeitungsprozess zurückgegeben. Der KI-Service wird nicht als Ersatz, sondern als Bypass zur bestehenden Eingangsverarbeitung eingeführt. Die Aussteuerung der Sendungen erfolgt über vom Beitragsservice bereitgestellte intelligente Weichen; die Kernsysteme bleiben unverändert. Nicht Gegenstand der Ausschreibung sind das Scannen bzw. die Digitalisierung der Sendungen, die Ein- und Ausgangsschnittstellen der Gesamt-Eingangsverarbeitung sowie die intelligenten Weichen selbst. Der Leistungsgegenstand gliedert sich in drei Bausteine: Baustein 1 - Cloud-Infrastruktur: Bereitstellung einer souveränen, hochverfügbaren und skalierbaren Cloud-Umgebung als IaaS einschließlich bedarfsgerecht skalierbarer CPU-, GPU-, Speicher- und Netzwerkressourcen für KI-Workloads. Es ist beabsichtigt, einen Vertrag über die Bausteine 1 und 2 mit einer 4-jährigen Festlaufzeit abzuschließen. Baustein 2 - Managed Service: Betrieb der KI-Plattform als PaaS und SaaS, insbesondere Monitoring, Logging, Incident- und Problem-Management, Patch- und Release-Management, Backup und Recovery, Kapazitätsmanagement sowie Bereitstellung und Betrieb eines standardisierten KI-Serving-Stacks (u. a. Container-Orchestrierung, Inferenz). Der Beitragsservice behält die Hoheit über Fachlogik, Agenten sowie Auswahl und Wechsel der KI-Modelle. Es ist beabsichtigt, einen Vertrag über die Bausteine 1 und 2 mit einer 4-jährigen Festlaufzeit abzuschließen. Baustein 3 - Entwicklung einer individuellen Input-Management-Lösung ("KI-Service"): Konzeption, Entwicklung, Integration und Produktivsetzung einer individuellen Lösung auf Basis der bereitgestellten Plattform, einschließlich Einrichtung von Klassifikation und Extraktion je Sachverhalt, Nachweis der vereinbarten Erkennungsqualität, Schulung, Dokumentation und Unterstützung der Abnahme. Der KI-Service inkl. sämtlicher Arbeitsergebnisse (u. a. Quellcode, Konfigurationen, Prompt-Artefakte, Datenmodelle, Schnittstellenbeschreibungen, Tests, Dokumentation) geht mit zeitlich, räumlich und inhaltlich unbeschränkten Nutzungsrechten auf den Beitragsservice über. Dem Beitragsservice ist zudem das Recht einzuräumen, den KI-Service uneingeschränkt zu nutzen, zu betreiben, zu verändern und weiterzuentwickeln sowie durch Dritte betreiben oder weiterentwickeln lassen können. Es darf keine Abhängigkeit vom ursprünglichen Auftragnehmer entstehen und ein Anbieterwechsel muss grundsätzlich möglich sein. Die Lösung ist vorrangig auf Basis von Open-Source-Komponenten mit permissiven Lizenzen zu realisieren. Ergänzend ist ein Dienstleistungskontingent für weitere Sachverhalte vergleichbarer Komplexität und für Optimierungen nach der Produktivnahme bzw. Abnahme vorzusehen. Fachlicher Umfang und Mengengerüst: Schwerpunkt sind rund 1,8 Mio. formlose Schreiben pro Jahr, die bislang weder automatisch klassifiziert noch inhaltlich ausgewertet werden. Hinzu kommen rund 4,7 Mio. formgebundene Schreiben aus fünf Sachverhalten: Befreiungen, Abmeldungen, Drittschuldnererklärungen, Klärungsverfahren aufgrund Sterbefall sowie Bank- und Adressänderungen. Für die Dimensionierung ist von mindestens 6,5 Mio. Sendungen pro Jahr auszugehen (ca. 25.000 Sendungen je Arbeitstag, Spitzenwert ca. 26.700). Der Handschriftanteil liegt bei ca. 20 %. Teilweise sind besondere Kategorien personenbezogener Daten nach Art. 9 DSGVO (z. B. Gesundheitsangaben) zu verarbeiten. Die Bereitstellung ist in folgende Leistungsbereiche aufgeteilt: - die Lieferung von Hardwarekomponenten für die ETERNUS CS8800 sowie die Switche für die Anbindung an die physische Tape Library; - die Erbringung von Dienstleistungen zur Installation, bei den Konfigurationen, der Anbindung der physischen Tape Library über die Switche und dem Cascading nach Ismaning beim Auftraggeber in Köln und den erforderlichen Konfigurationsarbeiten bis zur vollständigen Integration der neuen ETERNUS CS8800 und Switche; - die Durchführung von umfassenden Integrationstests; - die Durchführung der Migration der Daten von der bisherigen ETERNUS CS8800 auf die neue ETERNUS CS8800; - die Übereignung der neuen ETERNUS CS8800 und Switche; - die produktive Inbetriebnahme der neuen ETERNUS CS8800 und Switche bis hin zur Abnahme; - Rücknahme der zu ersetzenden ETERNUS CS8800 Hardware-Komponenten (Ausnahme: nicht flüchtige Datenträger müssen beim Auf-traggeber verbleiben). Nutzung, Gefahr und Lasten der neuen ETERNUS CS8800 und Switche gehen erst mit der Abnahme auf den Auftraggeber über. Mit der Bereitstellung der neuen ETERNUS CS8800 und Switche hat der zukünftige Auftragnehmer unverzüglich nach Zuschlagserteilung zu beginnen. title: Germany – Foreign economic-aid-related services – 10035573-Operationalization of the circular economy in Colombia
description: Green Jobs in the Circular Economy in Colombia III (PREVEC III) is a technical cooperation project implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), in partnership with key Colombian national institutions including the National Planning Department (DNP), the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (MinAmbiente) and the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism (MinCIT). Colombia's transition to a circular economy represents both an urgent climate imperative and a significant opportunity for sustainable economic development. PREVEC III responds to this challenge by supporting the development and scaling of climate-friendly circular economy business models in three priority sectors: textiles, tourism and agrifood, while promoting the creation of green and greened jobs and strengthening the conditions for sustainable production and consumption at national and subnational level. The project works across three interconnected areas: supporting companies to develop market-ready circular business models and access climate finance; facilitating technology transfer and innovation between German/European and Colombian partners; and translating project results into evidence-based policy dialogue at national and international level. It contributes to Colombia's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC), the national climate finance agenda and international frameworks including the Paris Agreement, the UN 10-Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Production and Consumption and the EU Green Deal. Results are tracked across five key dimensions: the regional scaling of circular economy business models beyond the main urban centres; small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) preparation for access to climate finance; the creation and verification of green and greened jobs with gender and vulnerability disaggregation; the application of circular economy innovations in Colombian enterprises; and corporate greenhouse gases (GHG) measurement and climate reporting. These dimensions are embedded in a results framework that links operational outputs to strategic outcomes, contributing to Colombia's climate commitments at national and international level. PREVEC III builds on a decade of GIZ engagement in circular economy in Colombia and is implemented together public institutions, private sector associations and subnational governments.

description: Die Auftraggeberin plant bundesweite Instandhaltungs- und Instandsetzungsmaßnahmen an Bestandswohnimmobilien. Gegenstand des vorliegenden Vergabeverfahren ist die Vergabe von Generalplanerleistungen an Wohnbestandsimmobilien und angemieteten Immobilien. Die von der Ausschreibung betroffenen Objekte sind insbesondere in der Auflistung der Objekte nach den jeweiligen Losen aufgeführt (siehe Anlage C-02b). Zum Leistungsgegenstand gehören auch die in den Objektlisten enthaltenen Gewerbe- und Sondergebäude. Die zu vergebenden Generalplanerleistungen umfassen insbesondere folgende Leistungen - Objektplanung Gebäude - Tragwerksplanung - Planung der Technischen Ausrüstung - Planung der Freianlagen - Planung und Beratung Bauphysik - Brandschutz einschl. Brandschutzkonzept - Koordination und Integration Gutachterleistungen - Weitere Leistungen nach Anlage C-01a und c. Je Los ist der Abschluss eines Rahmenvertrags mit zwei Rahmenvertragspartnern mit jeweils dem wirtschaftlichsten und zweitwirtschaftlichsten Bieter geplant, aus denen die Auftraggeberin sukzessiv Einzelaufträge jeweils stufenweise abrufen wird. Der Auftragnehmer hat weder einen Anspruch auf Abruf von Einzelaufträgen noch innerhalb eines vergebenen Einzelauftrags auf den Abruf aller ausgeschriebenen Leistungsphasen. Die konkreten Einzelheiten der Beauftragung ergeben sich aus der Rahmenvereinbarung und den Vereinbarungen zum Einzelauftrag. Der jeweilige Rahmenvertrag wird eine Laufzeit von 2 Jahren haben, wobei die Auftraggeberin nach Maßgabe des Vertrags durch einseitige Erklärung den Rahmenvertrag zweimal um jeweils ein Jahr verlängern kann. Die maximale Vertragslaufzeit beträgt 4 Jahre. Das jeweilige Ende der Laufzeit eines Einzelauftrags bleibt vom Ende der Rahmenvertragslaufzeit unberührt.
